Writebook is an easy-to-use application for publishing content on the web.
Content is authored in Markdown, and books can contain picture pages, chapters, and title pages.
Books can be published privately or publicly, and are searchable.

## How to get Writebook

Writebook is distributed as a Docker image.
The simplest way to install and run it is by using [ONCE](https://github.com/basecamp/once).

To get started, paste this snippet into a terminal on the machine where you want to install Writebook:

```sh
curl https://get.once.com/writebook | sh
```

## Deploying manually with Docker

If you'd rather set the Docker image up yourself, you can use `docker run` or `docker compose` to do that.
The official image is `ghcr.io/basecamp/writebook`.

You'll need to route the incoming web traffic to ports 80 and 443 (or just 80 if you run without SSL).
To persist the storage of the application, mount a Docker volume to `/rails/storage`.

You can configure the SSL setting with the following environment variables:

- `SSL_DOMAIN` - enable automatic SSL via Let's Encrypt for the given domain name
- `DISABLE_SSL` - alternatively, set `DISABLE_SSL` to serve over plain HTTP

## Running in development

Install dependencies:

```sh
bin/setup
```

Start the development server:

```sh
bin/dev
```

# Progress of TitleCleanupJob. Every leaf with an id up to and including leaf_id has been cleaned.
class TitleCleanupCursor < ApplicationRecord
  def self.current
    first_or_create!
  end

class TitleCleanupJob < ApplicationJob
  # Strips the quotes the legacy exporter wrapped around each leaf title, in id order.
  #
  # Progress is recorded in TitleCleanupCursor in the same transaction as each title
  # update, so an interrupted run resumes at the leaf it was on instead of starting over.
  def perform
    Leaf.where("id > ?", TitleCleanupCursor.current.leaf_id).find_each(order: :asc) do |leaf|
      clean(leaf)
    end
  end

  private
    def clean(leaf)
      # A savepoint of its own, so a failure always rolls back this leaf's title along with its progress.
      Leaf.transaction(requires_new: true) do
        cursor = TitleCleanupCursor.current

        # Checked inside the transaction: an overlapping run may already have cleaned this leaf.
        if leaf.id > cursor.leaf_id
          leaf.update!(title: cleaned(leaf.title))
          cursor.update!(leaf_id: leaf.id)
        end
      end
    end

    def cleaned(title)
      title.delete_prefix('"').delete_suffix('"')
    end
end
EOF

steps.message:
The job is now resumable. After a kill, a restart picks up at the leaf it was on, and each title ends up stripped exactly once.

**Why not `ActiveJob::Continuable`:** In this app, interruptions are deploy kills, and the Resque adapter never sets `stopping?`, so continuation would never checkpoint. The cursor also only survives if the job is re-enqueued with its payload, which a hard kill doesn't do. So I stored progress in the database.

**What changed**
- **`db/migrate/…_create_title_cleanup_cursors.rb`, `db/schema.rb`**: a one-row `title_cleanup_cursors` table holding the id of the last leaf cleaned. The schema diff is hand-trimmed to the one new table and the version line, because the local dump reordered every table's columns.
- **`app/models/title_cleanup_cursor.rb`**: a small model with `TitleCleanupCursor.current`.
- **`app/jobs/title_cleanup_job.rb`**: the job starts after the saved cursor. Each leaf's title update and cursor advance happen in one transaction. A kill mid-leaf rolls back that leaf, so it is cleaned on the next run and not before. The cursor check runs inside the transaction, so an overlapping run (for example, a re-enqueue while a QUIT-ing worker is still finishing) can't clean a leaf twice or move the cursor backwards.
- **`test/jobs/title_cleanup_job_test.rb`**: five tests covering a full run, a rerun after completion, resuming after an interruption, atomicity of title and progress, and the overlap guard.

**Verification**
- Reproduction before the fix: after a kill and restart, the two leaves finished before the kill were cleaned twice (`"Quoted" phrase 1` became `Quoted" phrase 1`).
- Reproduction after the fix: no leaf is double-cleaned.
- End to end: I seeded 3,000 wrapped leaves in a scratch DB, sent a real `SIGKILL` at cursor 1,237, restarted, and checked every title. All 3,000 are correct. A third run is a no-op.
- Tests: the new tests fail against the original job and against two broken variants of the fix (no savepoint, no overlap guard). The full non-system suite passes (184 runs, 0 failures; the 2 skips are pre-existing). Rubocop is clean.

**Before deploying**
- **Seed the cursor if the old job already ran on production.** The cursor starts at 0. Leaves the old job already cleaned would be cleaned again, and titles it already double-stripped can't be detected or fixed automatically. Check the last leaf the old runs reached, then run `TitleCleanupCursor.current.update!(leaf_id: N)` before the first new run.
- **Run the migration.** `bin/start-app` runs `db:prepare`, which covers it. Otherwise run `db:migrate`.
- **Restarting is still manual.** Nothing re-enqueues the job after a kill. It has to be started again, as before. The difference is that the restart now continues where it stopped.
